A little game of noticing

Can you tell?

One task. Two AI answers. One had a skill, the other a same-length fake. Read them, trust your hunch, then reveal.

This is not a test of you, or a measurement of the skill.

The fake is unrelated text with the same length as the skill instructions, not the answer.

A hunch stays a hunch

One reader's picks on these pairs. It is not a measurement of the file: it moves no verdict, and it says nothing about other readers, tasks or models.

These reports use a small set of text tasks per skill. Beating the fake is not beating no skill. In Report 018 the judge uses the same model as the target. Self-grading may favor its own model's answers.

About the answers and your privacy

These are whole, kept answers from Reports 017 and 018, matched by task and try. The builder checks the receipt, answer and task hashes. Those checks establish internal consistency, not who made the answers.

The fake is unrelated text cut to the same length as the skill instructions. Same length does not mean the answers have equal length. The twist uses that fake against no skill at all, from the same run.

Your picks never leave this page: it sends none of them, stores nothing and calls no model. The site's standard visit counter still counts the page view. Changing your selection clears your picks.

The page source holds which answer is which. Read the pairs before you read the source.
